en.title: Stress on the Last Syllable
en.summary: Learn how and when to stress the final syllable of Romanian words clearly and correctly.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: In Romanian, many words carry the strong beat on the last syllable. You hear this beat clearly at the very end of the word. Listen to (ajuns) /aˈʒuns/, which means arrived. The final part sounds louder and stronger. This gives the language a steady rhythm.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start the word with a relaxed mouth. Push more air from your lungs on the final syllable. Raise your voice pitch slightly on that last part. Make the last vowel longer and clearer. Listen to (copil) /koˈpil/, which means child.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Many Romanian words end in a consonant. These words often place the stress on the last syllable. Words that describe past actions usually do this too. Look at the word (oraș) /oˈraʃ/, which means city. Notice how the stress falls right at the end.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not stress the first syllable of these words. If you stress the beginning, the word sounds strange. Keep the first vowels light and short. Save your energy for the end of the word. Keep your pitch steady until you reach the final sound.
